chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who has two wives, one of whom is more beloved to him than the other: Is it permissible for him to favor one over the other? He said: 'Yes, he may favor some of them over others, as long as they are not four.' And he said: 'If a man marries a virgin while he has a divorcee (thayyib), he may favor the virgin by three days.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعاً: four (referring to the maximum number of wives)
key_terms.ثَيِّبٌ: a divorcee or widow (previously married wife)
key_terms.يُفَضِّلُ: to favor or give preference to

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for favoring one wife over another in terms of time distribution in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that 'equity' (adl) in polygyny refers to tangible divisions like time and wealth, rather than equal emotional love, which is beyond human control. It specifically permits a husband to allocate an extra three days to a virgin wife compared to a divorcee, reflecting the scholarly view that different marital statuses may warrant differentiated treatment in material rights. This ruling underscores the practical application of fairness within the four-wife limit, distinguishing between subjective affection and objective distribution.
